sources.title: Worker rights and protections (OSHA)
sources.by: US Department of Labor, Occupational Safety and Health Administration
sources.licenceSeen: The OSHA page itself shows no copyright line; the Department of Labor copyright page (dol.gov/general/aboutdol/copyright) says government-created material is 'generally part of the public domain' and may be used without permission.
sources.terms: No terms on the page about AI or automated use found; page footer links to Disclaimers and Important Website Notices that were not read.
sources.needIt: Tells any worker they can ask for safety training, refuse truly dangerous work, report hazards, and not be punished for it.
sources.notes: Covers rights to a safe workplace, training in a language you understand, safe machinery, protective equipment, injury records, confidential complaints and the 30-day whistleblower deadline. DOL seals and logos are not free to use. Check dates and phone numbers when building.

sources.title: Work, Employment, and Industrial Relations Theory (15.676, Spring 2008)
sources.licenceSeen: OCW course page footer links the Creative Commons licence; OCW Terms page states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
sources.terms: OCW Terms page: content may be used to train and improve AI models with attribution, non-commercial use only, and derived models must carry CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 or a compatible licence.
sources.needIt: Explains why bosses and workers want different things and how unions, laws and pay systems grew from that.
sources.notes: GRADUATE course; rebuild at an everyday level. OCW lists Lecture Notes and Written Assignments, no videos. Skip the theory jargon.

sources.title: Carpentry
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Explains tools, joints, framing and how a house goes together, so a person can talk to a contractor and do simple repairs.
sources.notes: First published 1916 (per Gutenberg page). Old tools and lumber sizes; no mention of modern safety gear; old finishes may be lead based. Flag for current safety guidance (OSHA, eye and hearing protection).

sources.title: Carpentry and Woodwork
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Step by step woodworking for beginners and school shops.
sources.notes: Old safety practice; add dust, guard and eye protection notes. Lumber grades and fasteners have changed.

sources.title: Modern Machine-Shop Practice, Volumes I and II
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Shows how metal parts were turned, drilled and fitted, which explains where every machine part comes from.
sources.notes: Very large, 19th century. Use only a few chapters. No modern guarding, coolant or lead and hazard knowledge; flag all shop practice as unsafe to copy without current training.

sources.title: Cyclopedia of architecture, carpentry, and building: a general reference work
sources.licenceSeen: Archive page shows date 1907 and no rights statement (only a Terms of Service link); public domain by age.
sources.needIt: A trade school course in book form: framing, roofs, stairs, plumbing and heating basics.
sources.notes: Volume 3 of a set. Includes old wiring, plumbing and heating (lead pipe, gas lighting, early electric), which are unsafe by today's code. Flag against current codes. Audit 16 Nov 2026: the item names no volume (the id suggests 3, its description cites Vol. 2); confirm on the item page before building. American Technical Society, Chicago, 1907.

sources.title: Practical blacksmithing
sources.licenceSeen: Archive page: 'Possible copyright status: The Library of Congress is unaware of any copyright restrictions for this item.'
sources.needIt: Shows forge work, heat and metal, the craft behind every tool, hinge and hook.
sources.notes: Coal forge and old fuel and fire practice; add current fire, eye and ventilation safety. Four volumes exist on Archive; this id is one clean copy.

sources.title: US Navy Training Course: Blueprint Reading and Sketching
sources.by: US Navy (author not named on page)
sources.licence: Not stated on page (appears to be a US Navy training manual)
sources.licenceSeen: Archive page shows no copyright or licence statement; date and author not named. US Navy training course by nature, but that is not stated on the page.
sources.needIt: Teaches how to read drawings, which every trade, repair job and home project needs.
sources.notes: LINK ONLY until the licence is confirmed on the document's own title page. Uploaded 2016 by a private uploader; confirm original NAVPERS or NAVEDTRA number. Audit 16 Nov 2026: no date, author or rights on the item, and a private uploader: link only, not a spine.

sources.title: Basic Electricity, NAVPERS 10086
sources.needIt: Explains electricity the way a Navy trainee learned it: circuits, wire, tools and safe work.
sources.notes: 1956 text: wire colors, insulation, and voltage rules are out of date; old materials may be hazardous. Flag all wiring advice against the current National Electrical Code and let electricians do house wiring.

sources.title: Letters from an Old Railway Official to His Son, a Division Superintendent
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Warm, practical advice on managing people, owning mistakes and running a crew, from a long-career boss.
sources.notes: Early 1900s railroad world and sexist language; rewrite to current workplaces and keep the principles.

sources.title: Business English: A Practice Book
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Drills for the writing a job needs: notes, messages and short letters.
sources.notes: Dated business forms (telegrams, carbon copies); replace with email.

sources.title: Mechanical drawing for industrial and high schools
sources.licenceSeen: Archive page: 'The Library of Congress is unaware of any copyright restrictions for this item.'
sources.needIt: Teaches how to draw an object so someone else can build it, the first step of any make.
sources.notes: Pencil, T-square and ink drawing; modern drawing is on a screen. Keep the lines, views and dimension rules.
